label: adult-s8
summary: The model predicts the probability of low income (the at-most-50k class) on the adult census data, with a training AUC of 0.911. It is mostly a linear model: the direct input edges carry most of the ranking (AUC 0.492 without them), led by marriage to a civilian spouse (direct weight -2.46 per sd), capital gains, education level, sex and hours worked, each lowering the predicted chance of low income in the expected direction. On top sit three kinds of nonlinear part. Capital-gain thresholds: two hinges open near 5000 US dollars of gains and remove a standing push towards low income, so the typical case falls from 59% with no gains to 0.01% with 15000 US dollars. A youth gate adds a push towards low income below about the median age except for other-service workers (17545 training rows have it on). Category switches add fixed pushes for single levels (never married for 12914 rows, widowed, tenth grade, self-employed, armed forces and a few countries of birth). Two switches are fitted to tiny groups and give certain predictions: armed forces (12 rows, predicted 0.0% although 9 have low income) and Honduras (14 rows, predicted 100.0%).
